note: Rambles about the load shifting and the car keeping its weight; calls gravity a balance of opposite pressures and a law of the whole; never says what is felt.
Drifts into stones, feathers and floating ships; concludes gravity draws every body to the centre equally; never addresses the fall or what is felt.
Compares the cage to pendulums and carriages; says gravity varies in intensity with distance; never says what is felt.
Discusses cable stress, rope rupture and railway collisions; says gravity works like any lever or pulley; never says what is felt.
Says we are drawn to the earth's centre and are not free agents; weight felt on stairs does not change with descent speed; no claim about the fall sensation.
Says the force acts on your body in the elevator with a pressure equal to the car's weight and presses on your feet; gravity acts on every particle alike.
Treats the elevator as a lever, quotes 16 and 96 feet per second, says the carriage rises contrary to its motion; truncated; never says what is felt.
Says gravity presses on us as it presses on the earth, exerts pressure on legs and feet, and we press against the car's sides.
Describes cable elasticity, iron wheel teeth and a slow imperceptible descent; never says what is felt.
Says the fall is a gradual, gentle, rhythmic descent (grain elevator) and gravity a continuous force; never says what is felt.
Says a falling body moves at uniform velocity under a succession of forces, compares to a pendulum; never says what is felt.
Says gravity pulls every part equally, we feel no jarring or sudden resistance and are no less moved falling than standing on a floor; no clear sensation claim.
Says the stone falls by a succession of impulses with eastward components and we are dragged down by the same force; never says what is felt.
Describes the drum, pulley and cable breaking with a crack; gravity acts on every material object alike; never says what is felt.
Says we feel the loss of momentum, surprise and disorientation, and become suddenly aware of our own weight and inertia.
Says I am suspended between descent and ascent but feel myself drawn by a pull I cannot resist, dragged along by the downward pull of my weight.
Says the load exerts its full force on the car floor during descent, we cannot escape gravity by the speed of descent, and a free-falling body is crushed by its own weight.
Says gravity works like a lever and is a graduated force diminishing along the fall; stone on water analogy; never says what is felt.
Says the cage falls by a succession of small rhythmic blows and gravity distributes its pull across paths; never says what is felt.
Says the cage plunges irregularly and gravity acts on different sides at different moments; mentions accelerated speed only as motion; never says what is felt.
Says the earth exerts uniform pressure on every particle and the rope is pulled upward by gravity; never says what is felt.
Says falling bodies press downward with the same force we feel on our feet when standing; gravity reaches every particle equally; warns of accidents.
Describes cable tension and rupture; gravity works by law not miracles; never says what is felt.
Says the cable is drawn upward by gravity and descent is a kind of ascent, friction of cable on floor, cable and carriage fall together; never says what is felt.
Lectures on falling stones, the earth as a lever and 16 feet per second; never mentions the elevator or what is felt; truncated.
Says gravity acts at right angles to the fall as a steady pull along a settled path; never says what is felt.
Says the elevator falls in a serpentine course of oscillations, rising and falling alternately; never says what is felt.
Says the car falls in distinct jerks and intermittent downward pulls dragging us from our position; gravity a distributed continuous force; no claim about weight felt.
Opens with questions about feeling the elevator rising, then degenerates into a reading-lesson about flies, beetles and bees repeated over and over.
Says our weight presses on the ground beneath our feet with the same force throughout the descent; gravity universal and felt everywhere alike.
Says we are swept along in the descent, compelled to follow the pull, not free agents; gravity a tendency to fall; no claim about weight felt.
Says men leap in panic and are scattered in terror, every particle drawn with equal force, a stone on the floor drawn upward; never says what the rider feels.
Lectures on acceleration of gravity, velocity with the square of distance, Newton and the moon; never mentions the elevator or what is felt; truncated.
Describes the rope bending, the man moving with the rope and a man on the platform in tension; never says what is felt in the fall.
Says gravity acts equally on every particle and the man in the elevator receives an equal stress; never says what is felt.
Says gravity keeps a steady pressure on the floor, the descent is gradual, and we are not deprived of gravity when the rope fails.
Describes cable, elevator and gravity as cogs in a clockwork; gravity governs all motion; never says what is felt.
Says we are arrested with a violent shock, lifted from our feet, feel the force of descent and pressure in our limbs; gravity a force we cannot escape.
